page: Amazon Web Services x2iezn.6xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro hypervisor instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8252C processor running at up to 4.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 24 dedicated vCPUs across 12 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, featuring 24 MB of L3 cache, hardware AES acceleration, and AVX-512 instruction support. System memory measures 768.0 GB of DDR4 operating at 3 GHz, delivering an extreme memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32 GB per vCPU. The instance bundles no local NVMe storage and includes no discrete GPUs, depending entirely on network-attached storage across a 50 Gbps baseline network link.

Benchmark results highlight strong memory subsystem throughput and data compression performance. In synthetic testing, the instance achieved a top-tier PassMark memory score of 2,899.68 alongside single-threaded gzip throughput of 31.88 GB/sec. Large-block memory bandwidth sustains 103.8 GB/sec for uncached reads and 49.0 GB/sec for writes. General computation tests, including Geekbench multi-core (11,173.0) and PassMark CPU (28,155.2), place the instance squarely within middle-tier averages, while Redis operations reached 25.57 million SET operations per second.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the platform delivers high value for RAM-dominated workloads that require fast per-core clock frequencies alongside massive volatile working memory. However, the lack of bundled local NVMe storage requires external EBS configuration for persistence, which must be factored into storage architectural design. Furthermore, execution of large language models shows steep performance degradation without hardware accelerators, yielding only 4.04 tokens/sec during 70B prompt ingestion.

The x2iezn.6xlarge instance is targeted at memory-intensive enterprise environments, particularly in-memory caching fleets, electronic design automation (EDA), relational and NoSQL memory databases, real-time analytics engines, and enterprise SAP HANA workloads.
